name: Argemone

watchlist.note: Useful Texas look-alike, especially farther north/west. Hold as watchlist rather than core until it becomes locally relevant.

genus_diagnostics.habit: Spiny annual or biennial herbs with glaucous foliage.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate, deeply lobed, with sharp marginal teeth/spines and often prickles on veins.
genus_diagnostics.sap: Colored latex is extremely useful for field identification.
genus_diagnostics.flower: Large white flowers in both current core species; numerous yellow stamens.
genus_diagnostics.sepals: Three caducous sepals forming a prickly bud, each with a horn-like tip.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Prickly capsule; prickle length, branching, and density are diagnostic.

quick_key.if: Fresh latex is light/pale yellow; sepal horns shorter and mostly unarmed; capsule prickles shorter and mostly unbranched
Fresh latex is orange to reddish-orange; sepal horns 8–12 mm and prickly; capsule prickles very long/unequal and often branched

study_warning: Both core species can have large white flowers. Do not identify them by flower color alone.

b073_study_strategy.warning: White-flowered Argemone can be deceptively similar. Do not separate A. albiflora from A. polyanthemos by flower color alone; use mature reproductive structures plus range.

quick_split: A. albiflora — large white flowers, glaucous prickly foliage, yellow latex; local PASS. Texas material commonly subsp. texana.
A. aurantiaca — existing south-central Texas anchor with yellow-orange flowers.
A. polyanthemos — white-flowered central/western plains species; target-zone range HOLD.
A. sanguinea — rose/red/lavender-flowered South Texas species; range HOLD pending 3 exact target counties.
